Apply Transformations

Source: R/transform_variables.R
transform_variables.Rd

Transforms the columns of a time-series object using the seven transformation codes of FRED-MD/FRED-QD.

Usage

transform_variables(x, code)

Arguments

x

a time-series object.

code

a named integer vector of transformation codes, one of 1:7 – see 'Details'. Names must match columns of x; a column with no entry is left untransformed (code 1).

Value

A time-series object of the same shape as x.

Details

The seven codes, applied column by column, are

1

no transformation, \(x_t\)

2

first difference, \(\Delta x_t\)

3

second difference, \(\Delta^2 x_t\)

4

logarithm, \(\log(x_t)\)

5

first difference of the logarithm, \(\Delta \log(x_t)\)

6

second difference of the logarithm, \(\Delta^2 \log(x_t)\)

7

first difference of the growth rate, \(\Delta(x_t / x_{t - 1} - 1)\)

Codes 4:6 need a strictly positive series.

A difference drops as many leading observations as its order – one for codes 2, 5 and 7, two for 3 and 6 – rather than shortening the series: those leading periods become NA, so every column keeps the time index of x and can still be combined with ts.intersect or passed to create_bvarmodel.

References

McCracken, M. W., & Ng, S. (2016). FRED-MD: A monthly database for macroeconomic research. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 34(4), 574–589.

McCracken, M. W., & Ng, S. (2021). FRED-QD: A quarterly database for macroeconomic research. Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Review, 103(1), 1–44.

See also

Other model set-up: add_initial_values.bvarmodel(), add_initial_values.bvecmodel(), add_priors.bvarmodel(), add_priors.bvecmodel(), combine_models(), create_bvarmodel(), create_bvecmodel(), use_expanding_window.bvarmodel(), use_expanding_window.bvecmodel()

Examples


data("us_macrodata")

code <- c(Dp = 2, u = 1, r = 2)
x <- transform_variables(us_macrodata, code)
